answer: Divergent Task State Divergence** Nodes broadcast their working memory state using an umber compression filter that reacts to parallel thread forks. When an agent duplicates, its twin processes output conflicting state proofs into the juniper validation mesh. The network detects this collision and forces both nodes to burn their local opal cache to resolve the split. The attacker pays a heavy bandwidth and processing penalty because every cloned agent instantly triggers a costly state collapse across the system.
